rationale:
bugs_open/225 — the evidence register guards COPY, not CODE, and a calculator ran an expired tax rule for sixteen months while every check passed. mortgagecalculator.co.uk's SDLT tool encoded the first-time-buyer relief cap that expired 2025-03-31; the site's prose and band table were correct, only the JS constant was stale. Nothing in the platform could catch it, and the three reasons are all deliberate design decisions: datahelpers/claims.go's nonAssertionElements drops <script> from every claims scan; editorialPageTypes exempts tool pages from the numeric arm; isExcludedNumber drops currency, so even the figure stated in finance PROSE is scanned by nothing. The one mechanism that reads raw rendered_html against the register (RFC_025's artifact_check) has zero consumers across 130 facts fleet-wide, is unreachable for citation-sourced facts (the citation branch continues before the artifact_check test), and is addressed by a component_id that had already died for this bug's own page when it was decomposed.

Meanwhile the register on that site carries 13 GOV.UK-cited SDLT facts, re-verified daily, whose governing_rule says in terms: 'A calculator is a claim about legislation: when a fact here changes or its citation is lost, every tool that encodes it is suspect until re-verified.' Nothing joined a fact to a tool. This change is that join, and it is not a new design: it is Pieces 2 and 3 of an owner-visible plan already in the repo (mortgagecalculator_couk_adoption/PLAN_2026-08-09_facts_into_tool_acceptance.md), whose Piece 1 is live as migration 366 / CLM-021. Piece 4 (an oracle computing expectations from the register) stays behind its RFC and is explicitly NOT in this change.

OPT-IN BY DATA, unsafe default OFF: until a tool's criteria fence carries a `facts` list, this code costs one extra SELECT per register-bearing site per day and changes nothing — no new action config key, no exported symbol changed, no schema change, no migration. Under the owner's RFC_022 narrowing (opt-in, unsafe side default OFF, zero live consumers — enumerated: 0 of 130 facts and 0 of 87 current tool PLANs declare anything today) this is council scope, not architecture scope.

THE PART I MOST WANT REVIEWED is the routing split, because getting it wrong is worse than not building it. A moved VALUE routes to tool-improver ONLY when a tool-level component owns the page's code AND the fence does not say no_auto_fix. Everything else — a non-fork page, a no_auto_fix fence, and EVERY evidence-only drift (citation lost, artefact changed) — routes to a human via a new handler-less fact_drift_review item. A fetch error routes to nobody at all. Two things drove that: bugs_open/281/TL-042 (tool-improver rewrites the SHARED template of a non-fork; one finding did exactly that fleet-wide on 2026-08-05 and again on 08-14), and bugs_open/126 (a false failure aimed an automated rewriter at a tool's disclaimer — here the target would be arithmetic on a page quoting tax law). Note the honest consequence: both live SDLT fences carry no_auto_fix and neither page is a fork, so on today's fleet EVERY route is human and the improve_tool arm is proven by unit test only. I would rather ship it that way than widen the auto-fix door.

MEASURED, and it changed the design: the fan-out deliberately does NOT use the acceptance ladder's toolEligibilityWhere predicate. Run live 2026-08-16, that predicate admits NEITHER tool this mechanism exists for — mortgagecalculator's tool-stamp-duty page carries two components and loanandmortgagecalculator's mortgages-stamp-duty three since its B2 decomposition, and the sole-component clause excludes both. Keying on eligibility would have produced a check that could never fire on the tools that motivated it, and it would have read green. It uses the platform's own name rule instead — the one Tier 4 already uses to resolve a tool's URL.

Every routing guard has a test that FAILS when the guard is removed: six mutations run, six reds, restored green (no_auto_fix, fork, evidence-vs-value, fetch-error, baseline-present, baseline-precedence), plus a seventh on the validator rule. The no-op path is asserted too — a site with no declaration costs exactly one SELECT and its result JSON is byte-identical to before.
submitter: bugs_open/225 class fix — register_guards_code_phase_b lane (Phase B of PLAN_2026-08-09_facts_into_tool_acceptance.md)

plan.summary: Join the evidence register to the tools that encode its facts. Piece 2: a tool's criteria fence may carry a fence-level `facts` list of register fact ids (ids only, never values — PBP-037's rule), shape-checked by a new validator rule P11. Piece 3: the daily evidence-freshness sweep resolves each site's declaring PLANs to its pages and files one work item per (fact, tool) that is owed something — improve_tool only where a fixer may safely act, a new handler-less fact_drift_review otherwise, and nothing at all on a fetch error. Opt-in by register/fence data; inert until a fence declares.

edits.rationale: Piece 2's parser. FENCE-LEVEL, not per-check: a tool encodes a fact, a check does not, and a per-check key stays refused by the validator's existing P7 inert-field rule. IDS ONLY, never values — pinning a value in a fleet-global doc_plans row (which has no site_id) would recreate the very failure the plan calls F3, a golden that defends a wrong number. FAIL-OPEN on absent/unparseable criteria, exactly like parseNoAutoFix beside it, so a fence that never mentioned facts cannot become an error elsewhere; a present-but-MALFORMED declaration returns issues so it is visibly ignored rather than silently dropped. Kept out of acceptanceFenceFlags deliberately: that struct is the judge's view, and a malformed facts value must not make parseNoAutoFix fail-open on a fence that set no_auto_fix correctly.

P11: refuse a malformed `facts` declaration WHERE IT IS WRITTEN rather than silently ignoring it on the day a fact moves — which is bugs_open/225's failure shape one rung higher. Placed after P5 and before the checks loop, so P7 still owns the per-check case. Nine lines, no behaviour change for any fence without the key. The doc comment's P1..P10 list gains P11, including the sentence that the key is read only by refresh_evidence_base and asserted by neither tier — so an author cannot read a green fence as 'the figures were compared'.

The site->PLAN->page join and the baseline. ONE query per register-bearing site, pre-filtered on the fence text; zero rows ends the pass. It resolves by the platform's OWN name rule (p.name IN (subject_key, 'tool-'||subject_key), plus a tool-level component whose function is the subject key) — the rule Tier 4 already uses for a tool's URL — and NOT by toolEligibilityWhere, which was measured live and admits neither of the two tools this exists for (both are multi-component pages). Fact ids resolve against the swept SITE's register, never the fleet-global PLAN (doc_plans has no site_id); an id the register does not carry is inert and reported, never fatal. The baseline is 'the value the tool was last TOLD': the latest fact_drift item's spec.fact.new_value for that (fact, tool), else the same fact's value in the site's PREVIOUS evidence_base row, else nothing fires. Read as a raw map, never through the typed EvidenceBase, which does not model citation/writer_line/unit. A per-fact 'last swept value' key in the register was rejected: it would make a consumer the author of a human-owned row.

The routing decision, pure and unit-testable in isolation (the shape a council objection forced on shouldRaiseStaleEvidence in the RFC_025 round, reused here deliberately). VALUE DRIFT -> improve_tool only when the page has a tool-level component AND the fence has no no_auto_fix; otherwise fact_drift_review with the reason recorded (not_a_fork / no_auto_fix). EVIDENCE DRIFT -> always human: a lost GOV.UK quote is not evidence a figure moved. FETCH ERROR -> reported, filed nowhere (CLM-008: unknown is not loss; an item on every 403 day trains people to ignore the queue). Two distinct item_key prefixes because refreshOnConflict rewrites an open item's summary and spec but never its type or handler — one prefix would let an open review item silently absorb a later auto-fixable finding.
edits.sketch:
switch {
case hasVal && baseline != nil && math.Abs(newVal-*baseline) > 1e-9:
    em.Kind = "value_drift"
    switch {
    case !tool.isFork():  em.Route, em.Reason = "fact_drift_review", "not_a_fork"
    case tool.NoAutoFix:  em.Route, em.Reason = "fact_drift_review", "no_auto_fix"
    default:              em.Route = "improve_tool"
    }
case entry != nil && entry.Outcome == "drifted":
    em.Kind, em.Route, em.Reason = "evidence_drift", "fact_drift_review", "evidence_drift"
case entry != nil && entry.Outcome == "error":
    em.Kind, em.Outcome = "skipped_unknown", "none"   // filed nowhere
    return em, true
default:
    return em, false
}

edits.rationale: The write half, one transaction per emission, through the SHARED writeWorkItem with refreshOnConflict (not a hand-rolled INSERT — the fork that bugs_open/091 was filed about). Each item carries page_id and, for a fork, component_id in the COLUMNS as well as the spec, because tool-improver's load_tool pre-flight hard-fails without page_id. The issue text is the payload the fixer actually reads ({{.input_data.issue}}), so it carries the fact id, old->new with unit, the register's own writer_line with {value} substituted, and the source URL — and, on a human route, the reason and what to do instead (re-file needs_tool_recreation, whose builder reads the register per CLM-021; never improve_tool, whose component_id would be the shared wrapper).
edits.sketch:
item := workItem{siteID: siteID, source: "scheduled", pipeline: "build", spec: string(specJSON),
    pageID: pageUUID, componentID: compUUID, createdBy: agentType, itemKey: em.ItemKey}
switch em.Route {
case "improve_tool":
    item.itemType, item.severity, item.priority = "improve_tool", "high", 30
    item.handlerAgent, item.status = "tool-improver", "detected"
default:
    item.itemType, item.severity, item.priority = "fact_drift_review", "medium", 35
    item.handlerAgent, item.status = "human-review", "needs_human_review"
}
write, err := writeWorkItem(ctx, tx, item, refreshOnConflict, logger)

edits.rationale: Two wiring lines and two omitempty result fields. The fan-out is PLANNED before the dry-run return (so a dry run reports exactly what it would file — that is how the live proof is run without writing) and WRITTEN after the two existing raises, so it cannot change when they fire. It never touches `changed`, res.Drifted, res.ArtifactCheckDrifted or shouldRaiseStaleEvidence: the RFC_025 round's architecture objection was that decoupling the citation raise altered behaviour for every existing caller, and that gate is left exactly as it is. A citation-only drift with nothing else changed still raises no site item; the per-tool item fires on its own trigger and its own key. EncodedByTools is stamped on drifted entries only, omitempty, so a site with no declarations marshals byte-identically to before (asserted by a test).

Thirteen tests, and the six that matter are induced reds: each routing guard was REMOVED in a scratch copy and the corresponding test failed, then the code was restored and all passed. That is the discipline this estate requires before a green means anything (a mock's own bookkeeping cannot assert a negative). Also asserted: the no-op site costs exactly one SELECT and its result JSON is byte-identical; a dry run marks its emissions dry_run and names the tool; a drifted fact stamps EncodedByTools; and the issue text carries everything the fixer needs, checked by content rather than assumed.

Classify the new fact_drift_review type ON THE WAY IN, in the same commit as its producer — this file's own 2026-07-20 correction, and necessary here because the SENSOR half only scans discovery_checks source and the producer lives in package actions, so neither half of the guard would ever see it. catJudgement rather than catMechanical: the item says a declared fact moved AND the tool may not be auto-rewritten, so every resolution is a person's (did the law change, must this tool's arithmetic follow, does a lost citation mean anything). There is no predicate to re-run — the daily sweep is the re-check, and it is the producer.
edits.sketch: "fact_drift_review": {catJudgement, "refresh_evidence_fact_drift.go (bugs_open/225 class) — a declared fact moved but the tool must not be auto-rewritten (not_a_fork / no_auto_fix / evidence_drift); carries page_id, and component_id when a fork exists. Resolution is a human ruling; the re-check is the daily evidence sweep itself"},

grounded_in: bugs_open/225 — "The lane's GOLDEN_2026-08-05_prechange.json records what every calculator answered on 2026-08-05 and golden_compare_post.py re-runs it. Those prove CONSISTENCY. calcSDLT has been wrong since it was written, so the golden recorded the wrong number faithfully and every comparison since has certified it. Nothing in the estate was asking whether the answer was RIGHT."

PLAN_2026-08-09_facts_into_tool_acceptance.md §0 — "the evidence register guards copy, not code. A fact constrains what a page may *say*; nothing connects a fact to the constants inside a calculator's JavaScript. mortgagecalculator.co.uk's original stamp-duty tool ran an expired tax rule for sixteen months and every check we own passed it."

PLAN_2026-08-09_facts_into_tool_acceptance.md §2 Piece 3 — "value drift (a re-derived number differs) -> improve_tool, carrying the fact's new value and writer_line in the spec. The tool must *change*. citation_lost / fetch error -> human review, never an automated rewrite. A 404 at GOV.UK is not evidence the number moved."
PLAN_2026-08-09_facts_into_tool_acceptance.md §5.1 — "doc_plans has no site_id. Resolve fact ids against the driven page's site, never against the PLAN."

site_specs evidence_base, mortgagecalculator.co.uk, governing_rule (live, re-verified 2026-08-15) — "This site's calculators and copy assert UK tax and product rules (SDLT bands, reliefs, surcharges)... A calculator is a claim about legislation: when a fact here changes or its citation is lost, every tool that encodes it is suspect until re-verified."

discovery_checks/check_tool_acceptance.go (the non-fork branch) — "tool-improver rewrites content_components.html_template, and for a ported instance that is the wrapper SHARED by every ported page on the site — an improve_tool from this very branch rewrote it fleet-wide on 2026-08-05 and again on 2026-08-14."

live DB, measured 2026-08-16 (the ladder's own eligibility predicate run over both SDLT sites) — "Neither mortgagecalculator's tool-stamp-duty (2 components) nor loanandmortgagecalculator's mortgages-stamp-duty (3 components since B2) is returned by toolEligibilityWhere — its sole-component clause excludes both. A fan-out keyed on eligibility could never fire on the tools that motivated it."

refresh_evidence_base_action.go, the stale_evidence raise gate — "a citation-only drift with nothing else auto-updating in the register still does NOT raise here — that is unchanged, ungated, pre-existing behaviour, and fixing it (if it should be fixed) is a separate, separately-reviewed change, not bundled into this one."
